claude_proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemRecord + magic_item kind
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: UnitRecord has no magic_item kind. SpellRecord, ClassFeatureRecord, and MasteryRecord all require domain-specific header fields (spell level/school, className/acquiredAtLevel, on_hit_trigger family) that are inapplicable to a magic item. A MagicItemRecord needs: id, name, provenance, description, item category (armor, weapon, wondrous, etc.), rarity, attunement requirement, and a MagicItemMechanics union.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Armor (Studded Leather Armor), Rare — neither a spell, class feature, nor mastery; has rarity and item-type metadata that no existing record type carries.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: passive_always_on family for MagicItemMechanics
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The +1 AC bonus is always active while wearing — no activation cost, no resource consumed, no trigger. All current families (activation, ongoing_effect, triggered_reaction, anchored_trigger, on_hit_trigger) require an activation event or spell-slot cost. A passive_always_on family would model 'while worn/attuned, effect X is permanently active' and emit a modify_ac (or modify_roll_numeric) atom attached to self with no procedure node.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: activated_property family for MagicItemMechanics
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The glamour property is a Bonus Action activation that applies alter_item_kind effect. It needs: bonus_action_quota consumed, alter_item_kind effect (v4 atom exists), and a novel expiry model ('until you use this property again or doff the armor'). No existing family covers item-property activations with unlimited-use (no use_count) bonus-action costs.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You can also take a Bonus Action to cause the armor to assume the appearance of a normal set of clothing or some other kind of armor.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: item_doffed expiry variant for lifecycle atoms
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The glamour lasts 'until you use this property again or doff the armor.' Neither turn_start_window, turn_end_window, rest_window, nor expire covers an equip/doff event. An item_doffed lifecycle event (or equip_window atom) is needed to represent 'ends when the item is removed'.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The illusory appearance lasts until you use this property again or doff the armor.
